title: Breast reconstruction: Role of Anastomosis site on Volume of lymphedema and Experience
summary:
After breast cancer surgery, some patients develop lymphedema—swelling of the arm that can significantly interfere with daily life. In breast reconstruction using the patient’s own tissue, the blood vessels of the graft must be connected to the body’s own vessels. This can be done either at the center of the breast or in the armpit area. It is not yet known whether the location of this vascular connection influences the development of lymphedema and quality of life.
The BRAVE study is investigating this prospectively in 74 patients across multiple clinics. Participation has no impact on the surgery or treatment. As part of regular follow-up appointments, arm circumference is measured, an ultrasound examination of the skin is performed, and quality-of-life questionnaires are completed at five time points (before surgery, on day 6, and after 6, 12, and 24 months).
conditions: Secondary arm lymphedema following treatment for breast cancer and its prevention in the context of microsurgical breast reconstruction.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Written informed consent
-    Completed primary curative treatment for breast cancer (with the exception of ongoing anti-hormonal therapy)
-    Following unilateral breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy (with or without prior reconstruction) with axillary intervention (sentinel lymph node biopsy [SNB] or axillary lymph node dissection [aLNE])
-    Planned microsurgical breast reconstruction using autologous tissue (DIEP or FCI), in which the anastomosis is to be performed on axillary vessels or on the internal mammary artery and vein
Exclusion criteria:
-    Expected lack of compliance or limited capacity to provide informed consent
-    Lack of written consent to participate in the study
-    Planned or ongoing oncological therapy during the observation period due to tumor recurrence (chemotherapy, radiation, or surgical re-intervention)
-    Pre-existing severe deformities of the affected limb or thorax that limit the standardized performance of measurements
